title: Grid container and tracks
learningObjectives: Explain grid container and tracks and build a responsive layout with it.

understand.concept: CSS Grid is a two-dimensional layout system for rows and columns. Setting display:grid or inline-grid creates a grid container; its in-flow children become grid items. Grid tracks are the rows and columns that define the grid structure.
understand.whyItMatters: Grid is useful when a layout needs control across both axes. Understanding explicit and implicit tracks helps explain where items are placed and why extra rows or columns appear.
understand.analogy: A grid is like a table of layout regions, but CSS Grid can place content into flexible tracks without requiring tabular HTML semantics.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; actual layout follows the flex or grid formatting algorithm.

explain.narrative: The first item spans both columns, while the next items occupy the two-column track structure.

examples.explanation: The first item spans both columns, while the next items occupy the two-column track structure.
examples.expectedOutput: A browser-rendered layout demonstrating the lesson concept.

practise.guidedTask: Create a two-column grid with a header spanning both columns and a main content area beside a sidebar.
practise.independentTask: Build a small responsive interface using the concept. Test long labels and more than one viewport width.
hints: Inspect the layout overlay in developer tools.
Change one container or item property at a time.
Check for overflow and preserve reading order.
